hyperedges.label: Recommended-profile code path (Reactor Context tenant propagation)
Three tenant-context antipatterns and their shared Reactor Context / lazy-resolution fix

nodes.label: Demonstrate antipattern command (curl with alternating X-Tenant-ID)
nodes.norm_label: demonstrate antipattern command (curl with alternating x-tenant-id)
nodes.rationale: Which pooled worker picks up a request is non-deterministic, so output varies between runs: either a 500 (context lost) or a 200 with tenant 1's users for tenant 2's request (wrong data).

nodes.label: integration-tests Maven profile (Failsafe, _IT classes)
nodes.rationale: _IT classes boot a real Spring context and HTTP server and are wired through Failsafe so they only run under the integration-tests profile and never slow ./mvnw test.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant context propagation
nodes.rationale: WebFlux execution hops across threads (subscribeOn, thread pools, event-loop workers), so per-thread state such as ThreadLocal cannot reliably carry request-scoped state like the current tenant through a reactive pipeline.

nodes.label: Runtime switching via Spring profiles (antipattern / recommended)
nodes.norm_label: runtime switching via spring profiles (antipattern / recommended)
nodes.rationale: The same feature is implemented twice, wrong way and recommended way, and selected at runtime by profile; application.yaml defaults spring.profiles.default to antipattern.

nodes.label: Antipattern 3: Eager evaluation of per-subscription state
nodes.norm_label: antipattern 3: eager evaluation of per-subscription state
nodes.rationale: getUser(long id) reads the tenant context synchronously at call time, before the Mono is built; if the context changes before subscription, the stale already-baked-in tenant is used.

nodes.label: Lazy resolution via Mono.defer / Mono.deferContextual
nodes.rationale: Deferring resolution means the tenant is read at subscription time (per-subscription, not per-call), making it immune to thread hand-off and to context changes between call and subscription.

nodes.label: Reactor Context propagation (contextWrite)
nodes.rationale: Reactor Context travels with the subscription instead of the thread, so request-scoped state survives thread hand-off regardless of which thread executes the work.

nodes.label: Antipattern 2: Stale data from reusing a pooled thread's inherited context
nodes.norm_label: antipattern 2: stale data from reusing a pooled thread's inherited context
nodes.rationale: An InheritableThreadLocal is copied only once, when a worker thread is created; a pooled boundedElastic worker that inherited tenant A keeps serving tenant A's data after the request thread moved to tenant B, returning wrong-tenant data rather than an error.

nodes.label: Antipattern 1: ThreadLocal/InheritableThreadLocal for request-scoped state
nodes.rationale: The filter stores the tenant in a ThreadLocal and relies on it still being present, but WebFlux hops threads (subscribeOn, pooled schedulers) and a plain ThreadLocal does not travel with the execution.
